findings.title: Momentary absence after ambiguous create is not completed cleanup
findings.scenario: Create client times out and is killed while daemon may still be processing its request. New cleanup accepts a single exact-name absence response and writes ownedContainerAbsent:true, then assertAvailable succeeds. A delayed daemon create can leave a container after the host has admitted another run. The same ambiguity applies to output-limit/transport failure.
findings.reproduction: Reused existing labelled absent CLI fixture, changing create to remain alive until the real invocation timeout. No daemon or generated code ran. Observed timeout diagnostic, STATIC_FAILED, cleanup true and capability available; captured in timeout-observation.log.
findings.repair: Only classify absent as completed cleanup after a definite completed failed-create response. For timeout/transport/output-limit ambiguous outcomes, keep cleanup fail-closed unless the exact owned container is positively identified, removed and absence verified. Preserve original finite failure separately. Add focused ambiguous-outcome regression.
